candidates: In CSF Next story snippets that reference another story's args for composition, access them via `.input.args` (e.g., `...Primary.input.args`), not `.args`. The `.args` property is CSF 3 syntax; in CSF Next the exported story's configuration lives under `.input`. The project codemod at `code/lib/cli-storybook/src/codemod/helpers/story-to-csf-factory.ts` confirms `.input.args` as the standard.

Every CSF Next code snippet that calls `preview.meta()` must also export at least one story created with `meta.story({...})`, or at minimum include `export default meta;`. A snippet that defines only `const meta = preview.meta({...})` with no further exports is non-functional and will not render any stories in Storybook.

Storybook APIs that only exist in the Node.js build of a framework package (e.g., `defineMain`) must be imported from the `/node` subpath entry point (e.g., `import { defineMain } from '@storybook/angular/node'`), not from the package root.

In TypeScript CSF Next snippets that call mock methods (`.mockReturnValue()`, `.mockImplementation()`, etc.) on auto-mocked modules, wrap the module with `mocked()` from `storybook/test` before calling mock methods (e.g., `mocked(uuidv4).mockReturnValue('...')`). Apply this consistently across all TypeScript renderer variants in the same snippet file.

When a snippet file is used in documentation for a specific builder (Vite or Webpack), only include renderer variants that actually support that builder. Storybook does not officially support Angular with Vite (any Angular+Vite integration is community-provided), and Web Components only supports Vite. Do not add mismatched renderer+builder combinations such as Angular variants in Vite builder documentation or Web Components variants in Webpack builder documentation.

Configuration options that require a specific Storybook builder (e.g., TypeScript `checkOptions` requires Webpack, available only in `@storybook/react-webpack5` and `@storybook/angular`) must only appear in snippets for frameworks that ship with that builder. Before adding a framework variant for a config option, verify the option is actually exported from the published package.

Story export names must be identical across all renderer variants within the same snippet file. If the React variant exports `Primary`, then Angular, Vue, Web Components, and Svelte variants in the same file must also export `Primary`, not `Default`, `Text`, `ExcludeStory`, or any other name.

When a snippet file contains both CSF 3 and CSF Next code blocks for the same renderer, every code fence must include a `tabTitle` attribute (e.g., `tabTitle="CSF 3"` or `tabTitle="CSF Next 🧪"`). Omitting `tabTitle` from any variant in a file that mixes CSF versions causes the docs site to render incorrect or missing tab labels.

In CSF Next snippets, always use `meta.story({...})` with an explicit (possibly empty) configuration object rather than `meta.story()` with no arguments. Do not mix the two forms within the same documentation set.

When adding CSF Next snippet blocks for Angular, Vue, or Web Components, also add explicit CSF 3 snippet blocks with the corresponding `renderer="angular"`, `renderer="vue"`, or `renderer="web-components"` attribute for the same feature. Relying solely on a `renderer="common"` CSF 3 block causes the docs site to display the generic snippet instead of the framework-specific one when those renderers are selected.
Svelte component story snippets must use a default import from the `.svelte` file (e.g., `import Button from './Button.svelte'`), not a named import from a `.js`/`.ts` file.

In Testing Library interaction test snippets, use the `name` option—not `text`—when filtering by accessible name in `getByRole` queries (e.g., `canvas.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' })`). The `text` option is not a valid `getByRole` filter and will silently fail to match any elements.

In CSF Next story snippets, import the Storybook preview module via an absolute or subpath import (e.g., `import preview from '#.storybook/preview'`) rather than a file-relative path (e.g., `import preview from '../.storybook/preview'`). Relative paths break when story files are moved to a different directory depth; see the CSF Next docs for configuring subpath imports.

In Vue CSF Next story snippets, the `render` function must receive args as a direct parameter (e.g., `render: (args) => ({...})`), not destructured from a context object (e.g., `({ args })`). The destructured form is not the correct Vue render function signature for Storybook story factories.

The MSW addon (`msw-storybook-addon`) is an older plugin without CSF Next `definePreview()` annotations support. Do not document it as `addons: [addonMsw()]` inside a `definePreview()` call; configure it via the CSF 3 / `main.js` style only.

In Vue and Web Components CSF Next `definePreview()` snippets, add a comment above the framework-specific import noting the available builder variants (e.g., `// Replace with @storybook/vue3-webpack5 when using Webpack`). This matches the placeholder pattern used in React examples and prevents users from assuming the Vite package is the only option.

Web Components story snippet meta objects should omit the `title` property and rely on Storybook's automatic title inference. Adding `title` is seldom needed in web-components examples and is inconsistent with the rest of the web-components documentation.

Before adding a TypeScript type import from a framework package's `/node` subpath (e.g., `@storybook/vue3-vite/node`), verify that the type is actually exported from that entry point. For example, `StoriesEntry` is not exported from the Vue 3 or Web Components node packages, and referencing it there produces a TypeScript compilation error.
Remove all unused imports from documentation snippets. For instance, do not include `import type { StoryObj }` if no `Story` type alias is used anywhere in that snippet.

The `filename` attribute in documentation snippet code fence headers for story files must include the `.stories.ts` or `.stories.js` extension (e.g., `filename="Button.stories.ts"`), not just the component file extension (e.g., `filename="Button.ts"`).

When a documentation snippet file includes both TypeScript and JavaScript CSF Next variants of the same feature, all argument names must be identical between the two variants. Mismatched arg names (e.g., `background` in TS vs. `backgroundColor` in JS) appear to document different component APIs to readers.

Order imports in documentation snippets as: (1) built-in/platform imports, (2) Storybook packages, (3) other third-party packages, (4) relative imports sorted from farthest to nearest. This matches the project's ESLint import-order configuration.

Proofread all code in documentation snippets for syntax errors and typos, including: duplicate keywords in import statements (e.g., `from  from`), missing commas in array or object literals, and spelling errors in inline comments.

In CSF Next snippets, use `meta.story({...})` when creating a new story from scratch. When a story should inherit from and modify an existing one, use the `.extend()` method (e.g., `Primary.extend({ args: {...} })`). Apply the same inheritance strategy consistently across all framework renderer variants in a snippet file.

Angular component imports in story snippets should reference the Angular CLI-generated kebab-case file name (e.g., `import { Button } from './button.component'`), not PascalCase (e.g., `'./Button.component'`), following Angular's file naming convention.

In Angular `applicationConfig` provider array documentation, ensure all array elements are properly comma-separated. When two providers are alternatives (e.g., `importProvidersFrom(BrowserAnimationsModule)` vs. `provideAnimations()`), document the choice explicitly with a comment (e.g., `// Or, alternatively:`) or show them in separate snippets to avoid implying both are simultaneously required.
